text:
meera: heads-up — noticed a correlated perf dip for several tenants on rack-r3u12 around 02:10 UTC. latency p50 jumped ~60% for short generations.
ops-bot: alert: GPU temp spike detected on rack-r3u12: gpu0=92C gpu1=90C gpu2=88C; cooling-fan=95% — throttling events logged.
alex: ouch. are those tenant workloads heavy decode loops or long ctxs?
meera: mix — small streams and some long-context chat tests. KV cache misses looked normal. saw a cluster-level ramp in per-tenant batch size around the time.
samir: got logs:
```
2026-11-02T02:09:58Z rack-r3u12 gpu0 throttle_count=3 avg_freq=900MHz target_freq=1500MHz
2026-11-02T02:10:12Z tenant=acme-qa batch_size=48 model=gpt-xl seq=2048
```
lia: interesting — acme-qa was routed to a shared pool (pool-shared-eu2), but we also had a couple of dedicated pools low on utilization.
meera: thought: is this a noisy neighbor thermal cascade? one tenant sending large batches warms rack, fans spin, adjacent GPUs throttle and drop perf for others.
alex: we saw similar last year but at pod level; never thought about rack thermal propagation. do we have thermal topology mapped?
samir: partial mapping in infra runbooks. rack r3 uses front-to-back airflow; neighbor effect likely. can reproduce in staging by running sustained 50% duty decode on one card.
meera: short term: can we add routing policy to prefer spreading heavy batches across racks when temp > 80C instead of packing into same rack? rule could be "rack_spread_on_temp".
lia: also consider tenant shaping: cap batch_size for shared pools when rack temp rising, or move the offending tenant to dedicated pool if available.
alex: pros/cons: spreading reduces heat per rack but increases cross-rack network egress and KV cache misses (cost). moving to dedicated avoids noisy neighbor but costs $$$. need cost calc.
meera: quick numbers: cross-rack egress adds ~3ms p95 on our tests, KV miss increases token compute by ~4%. moving to dedicated pool estimated +$X/hr.
samir: propose immediate mitigations: 1) temporary routing rule: avoid scheduling batch_size>32 on racks with avg_gpu_temp>82C 2) auto-evict top offender if one tenant is >40% of rack load 3) add short-term canary: slowly redirect one large tenant to dedicated to measure delta.
lia: +1 to canary. also add a short cooling cooldown: mark rack as soft-drain for 2m after throttle event to let temps drop.
meera: I'll prototype the routing rule in the router service tonight (simple check on pool selection). if someone can draft the eviction heuristic and cost comparison I'll roll together.
alex: I can run cost perf numbers and a rough dashboard of trade-offs. samir can you add the soft-drain TTL to rack state and hook to telemetry?
samir: on it. will add `rack_state.cooldown_ttl` and emit metric `rack.cooldown.active=1` when set. will add unit test to ensure eviction doesn't spam.
meera: thanks. follow-ups: after the canary, we should consider a long-term strategy: intelligent placement aware of thermal neighbors (heat-aware packing), or offering thermal isolation guarantees for dedicated pools.
lia: also file a customer impact note for accounts X/Y that saw degraded latency — keep it proactive.
alex: noted, I'll draft a short blurb for CS.
meera: ok team, timeline: prototype router change tonight, cooldown TTL by EOD tomorrow, canary run early tomorrow. tagging @lia for customer comms. :thumbsup:
ops-bot: scheduler: created issue INFRA-4987 "rack thermal spread routing rule" assigned to meera.
meera: thanks — I'll link the PR when ready.
alex: thanks all.
